ATTORNEY-CLIENT PRIVILEGED / ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
MEMORANDUM
To: Sarah Kowalski, VP Regulatory Affairs, Pinnacle Therapeutics (cc T. Kelling, D. Forsythe)
Re: Gap analysis, Protocol PTX-4820-201 v3.0 (May 18, 2025) and Appendix A ICF, against 21 CFR Parts 312/50/56/11, ICH/FDA guidance and the April 2, 2025 Pre-IND minutes

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The protocol is not IND-ready. Six FDA recommendations that Pinnacle accepted as action items (minutes, Section 6) are not implemented: DSMB, pathology panel, 30 mg titration, MELD exclusion, study-level stopping criteria, and interim/futility design. Yet Protocol 2.1 says the recommendations "have been incorporated... where appropriate", which is inaccurate. The minutes warn that no DSMB commitment could contribute to a clinical hold under 21 CFR 312.42. The ICF omits mandatory elements, the protocol has no pregnancy or contraception provisions, and the sample size is arithmetically wrong. Our draft checklist is unreliable (Section 5). Totals: 8 Critical, 9 Major, 4 Minor. September 15 is achievable only if Trident amends now and Ridgeway receives the ICF in final form.
Severity: Critical = likely hold or subject-safety/consent defect; Major = probable FDA deficiency; Minor = housekeeping. 21 CFR is binding; ICH, guidance and the minutes are non-binding but Pinnacle agreed to the action items.

2. CRITICAL FINDINGS
1. DSMB discretionary (Prot. 9.4, 10.3, 13.3). Protocol: DSMB "may be convened at the Sponsor's discretion"; sponsor retains ultimate responsibility. Minutes 4.4: mandatory, independent, charter before first subject, hepatologist/biostatistician/clinical pharmacologist, reviews after first 90 subjects, at interim, on signals, ad hoc, with authority over doses, arms, enrollment and the study. Fix 9.4: "An independent DSMB will be established and operational before the first subject is enrolled, under a written charter finalized before enrollment specifying membership (a board-certified hepatologist, an independent biostatistician and a clinical pharmacologist, without conflicts), review schedule, access to unblinded data by arm, voting rules, and authority to recommend dose modification, arm termination, suspension of enrollment or study termination. The Sponsor will give serious, good-faith consideration to, and promptly implement, DSMB recommendations." Conform 10.3 ("if convened").

2. Interim analysis (Prot. 10.3). Protocol: one efficacy interim at Week 26 of the last enrolled subject (about April 2027), no futility. Minutes 4.6/Action 1(f): interim at about 50% enrollment (about 180 subjects), formal futility at 20% conditional power with arm-level discontinuation, independent firewalled statistician, rules prespecified before enrollment (see also FDA Adaptive Designs guidance, Nov 2019). The protocol's "approximately 0.003" interim alpha at 50% information also looks low for an O'Brien-Fleming bound (about 0.0056 two-sided by my calculation); the SAP must specify it. Retaining Week 26 requires a Type C meeting; the 30-day window to dispute the minutes has lapsed.

3. Single-reader pathology (Prot. 8.1). One central pathologist, calibrated with the "Sponsor's medical team" (independence concern). Minutes 4.1: at least two independent hepatopathologists, third-reader adjudication, prespecified qualifications, blinding to arm, visit and other readers, disagreement definition (any fibrosis-stage discordance or NAS difference of 2 or more), adjudication process and calibration. FDA called single-reader assessment unacceptable for the primary endpoint. Fix 8.1 and the SAP; remove the sponsor calibration role.

4. No reproductive-safety provisions. WOCBP is defined but no pregnancy test appears in Table 4/App. C, and there is no contraception requirement for women or men, partner-pregnancy procedure, or fetal-risk language; 9.5.1 only stops drug on pregnancy. See ICH M3(R2) and 21 CFR 312.23(a)(6)(iii)(g) (measures to minimize risk). Minutes 4.7 also call for completed reproductive-toxicology results in the IND; their status is unknown. Fix: serum hCG at screening and Day 1, regular urine tests thereafter, highly effective contraception through Week 64, pregnancy follow-up. Confirm with Dr. Anand whether embryo-fetal studies exist; if not, consider excluding WOCBP.

5. ICF missing required elements (verified against 21 CFR 50.25):
- (a)(5) confidentiality and possible FDA inspection: absent (Prot. 11.4 has it; ICF does not).
- (a)(6) injury compensation/treatment (more than minimal risk): absent, though Prot. 13.4 describes insurance.
- 50.25(c) ClinicalTrials.gov statement: absent, though Prot. 13.6 commits to registration. It must be verbatim: "A description of this clinical trial will be available on http://www.ClinicalTrials.gov, as required by U.S. Law. This Web site will not include information that can identify you. At most, the Web site will include a summary of the results. You can search this Web site at any time."
- (b)(1) unforeseeable embryo/fetal risk; (b)(4) consequences of withdrawal and orderly termination; (b)(5) new significant findings: absent.
- (a)(2) risks omit liver injury/DILI (an AESI and FDA's central concern) and reproductive risk.
- (a)(1) duration wrong (Item 6); procedures omit PK sampling, biomarker/PNPLA3 genetic testing and the MRI-PDFF subset, and describe follow-up only as "check your health"; no HIPAA authorization although Prot. 11.4 promises one.
Proposed language: "Records identifying you will be kept confidential to the extent permitted by law. The FDA, the Sponsor and its representatives, and the IRB may inspect your records." "If you are injured as a direct result of this study, medical treatment will be available. [State who pays and the limits.] You do not give up any legal rights by signing."

6. ICF duration misstatement. ICF: "approximately 12 months." Protocol: 52 weeks treatment plus 12 weeks follow-up = 64 weeks from randomization (about 14.7 months); 72 weeks (about 16.6 months) including up to 8 weeks screening. Our June 18 email called 64 weeks "about 16 months"; that is incorrect. Suggested: "about 64 weeks (about 15 months) after your first dose, plus up to 8 weeks of screening, with up to 17 visits after randomization."

7. Sample size (Prot. 10.1, Table 5). Stated inputs (30% vs 45%, two-sided alpha 0.05, 80% power) require about 162 evaluable subjects per arm by the standard two-proportion formula, not 78; at 78 evaluable, power is about 50%. With 15% attrition, about 191 randomized per arm. FDA called the assumptions "generally reasonable" but did not recompute; do not rely on that. An underpowered design risks a "clearly deficient" finding (312.42(b)). Fix: biostatistics (Dr. Lattimore) to recompute and amend N, effect size or objectives. My check is arithmetic only.

8. 30 mg titration (Prot. 5.2, Table 3). Two weeks (5/15/30 mg) against FDA's minimum four weeks (5, 10, 15, then 30 mg from Week 4), found "insufficient"; agreed Action 1(b). Revise Table 3, ICF and 5.5 (a 10 mg strength is new, so check supply/blinding with Kensington).

3. MAJOR FINDINGS
9. MELD (Prot. 4.2). No numeric criterion; "history of hepatic decompensation" is subjective. Add exclusion of MELD of 15 or more at screening (Action 1(c)). Also add washouts for amiodarone, methotrexate, tamoxifen and high-dose acetaminophen and permitted-medication rules (minutes 4.3).
10. Study-level stopping and liver monitoring (9.2, 9.5, Table 4). Hepatic decompensation events are AESIs but have no aggregate triggers. Add prespecified thresholds (FDA example: 2 or more events in any arm, or significant imbalance versus placebo) triggering expedited DSMB review (minutes 4.5). FDA asks LFTs every 2 weeks to Week 12 then monthly; protocol has CMP only at Weeks 2, 4, 8, 12, then every 4 to 6 weeks, INR at Weeks 12, 24, 52 only. Add Weeks 6 and 10, monthly thereafter, INR with each panel; define permanent discontinuation after rechallenge.
11. Chronic toxicology gate. Minutes 4.7/Action 3: 39-week non-rodent study started before dosing, data in hand before any subject is dosed beyond 26 weeks, commitment in the IND cover letter. Protocol mentions only 26-week studies. Add the 26-week dosing gate. I did not review toxicology data.
12. Biopsy adequacy (8.1). Protocol uses 20 mm and 11 portal tracts, stricter than FDA's 1.5 cm and 6. Not noncompliant, but may raise missing primary data; inadequate-sample handling is only "consider obtaining an additional specimen". Prespecify repeat-biopsy offer, window and analysis handling (Action 4).
13. Safety reporting (9.1). Sponsor reporting is only "as required by applicable law". 21 CFR 312.32(c) requires IND safety reports within 7 calendar days for unexpected fatal or life-threatening suspected adverse reactions and 15 calendar days for other serious unexpected ones. The 48-hour investigator SAE window conflicts with 312.64(b) ("immediately"); use 24 hours. State timelines and the unblinded safety team. Not Critical because 312.32 binds the sponsor regardless of protocol text.
14. Part 11/EDC (12.1). TrialVault is described only by edit checks and role-based access: no validation, audit trail, e-signature, backup or Part 11 statement, though FDA flagged it. Add provisions; sponsor remains responsible (312.52).
15. Canadian sites (2.2, 11.2, 13.1). Six of 28 sites; Sections 2.2 and 13 cite only FDA. Agree: Major. Proposed 2.2 text: "For Canadian sites the study will also be conducted in accordance with the Food and Drug Regulations, Part C, Division 5 (Drugs for Clinical Trials Involving Human Subjects), the Tri-Council Policy Statement (TCPS 2) and ICH GCP. No Canadian site will enroll until a Clinical Trial Application has been filed with Health Canada and no objection received (30-day default review), and the Research Ethics Board of record has approved the protocol and a Canadian ICF." Proposed 13.1 text: the CTA is a separate submission; Canadian amendments, safety reporting and site activation follow Division 5. Engage Canadian counsel.
16. Statistics (10.2 to 10.5). No ICH E9(R1) estimand though FDA asked; mITT primary population excludes subjects lacking a Week 52 biopsy, with missing-at-random imputation only in sensitivity analysis. Add an estimand table and align multiplicity.
17. Misstatement of alignment (2.1). Correct once items above are fixed.

4. MINOR
18. ICH E6: FDA issued E6(R3) as final guidance on September 8, 2025; the protocol cites E6(R2). Decide which governs at submission.
19. FDA listed FibroScan and weight at Weeks 26 and 52; protocol uses Week 24 and Week 52 (weight Week 52 only). PNPLA3 and MRI-PDFF are not in the schedule.
20. Protocol cites 45 CFR 46.114(b); FDA-regulated research follows 21 CFR Part 56.
21. Minutes call the target "GVP"; protocol says GIP. Ask the FDA project manager to correct the record.

5. DRAFT CHECKLIST
Do not deliver the xlsx. It describes a different protocol: version 2.0 dated April 2024, doses of 50/150/300 mg, an Ishak primary endpoint, ANCOVA, an established DSMB, 24-hour SAE reporting, 3 biopsies, 40 sites, and ICF sections (HIPAA, genetics) not in Appendix A. It cites 312.23(a)(6)(iii)(h)-(m), which do not exist (the paragraph ends at (g)). Rebuild it against v3.0.

6. NEXT STEPS
Week 1: biostatistics recalculation; WOCBP decision; Trident drafts Protocol v4.0. Week 2: ICF to Ridgeway in final form; DSMB charter and SAP drafts; Canadian counsel. Share only redlines, not this memorandum, with Trident or Ridgeway (privilege).

7. LIMITS
eCFR and Cornell were blocked. Regulatory timelines and ICF elements were confirmed through search results and my knowledge of the text; verify pinpoint quotations before external use. Not reviewed: IB, CMC, nonclinical data.
